title: AI Programming Tutor with Course-Notes Retrieval and Hint-First Guidance

nodes.label: Learner web app
nodes.description: Lets a learner ask programming questions, shows hints and permitted solutions, and displays which course notes grounded each answer.

nodes.label: Conversation tutor service
nodes.description: Owns the tutoring session: receives the learner question, requests note retrieval and a hint decision, prompts the model, and returns the final grounded reply.

nodes.label: Hint and solution policy service
nodes.description: Decides per question whether to give a hint, a Socratic question, or allow a full solution, and enforces hints-before-solutions on every reply.

nodes.label: Course notes retrieval service
nodes.description: Searches approved course notes for passages relevant to the question, scopes results by course and version, and returns them with provenance.

nodes.label: Approved course notes store
nodes.description: Stores the versioned, instructor-approved course notes and search index; it is the only source the tutor may ground answers on.

nodes.label: Model gateway
nodes.description: Builds the prompt from the question, hint decision, and retrieved notes; calls the external LLM; validates that responses use only supplied notes or abstains.

nodes.label: Course notes curation
nodes.description: Lets instructors submit, review, approve, and version course notes, and invalidates stale versions so the tutor retrieves only current approved material.

nodes.label: Tutor logs and audit store
nodes.description: Records questions, retrieval results with note versions, hint decisions, model replies, and abstentions for audit and instructor review.

assumptions: The tutor serves one course; approved notes are curated by instructors and loaded offline into a versioned store.
An external hosted LLM API generates text; calls are read-only and no learner data is written to any external system.
Hints are required before any full solution; the tutor withholds complete solutions until the hint policy allows release.
No automatic model, prompt, or index update loop exists; content and prompt changes are human-reviewed and released manually.
